summary: Repeating one block is a valid idea in recurrent transformer designs. Here three laps reveal stored pictures of 3 + 4 = 7; no transformer block or arithmetic inference runs.

claims.claim: Transformer computation can repeat across depth.
claims.how: The single block and returning track illustrate a recurrent-depth architecture.

sources.title: Universal Transformers
sources.says: Transformer computation can recur across depth, with an optional mechanism that adapts the number of updates.

claims.note: This is the general idea; it does not reproduce every mechanism of a Universal Transformer.

claims.claim: The toy ends with the correct arithmetic statement 3 + 4 = 7.
claims.how: The five stored marks are 3, +, 4, =, 7; the last tile images contain only finished bitmap values.

sources.title: Multilayer perceptrons
sources.says: Hidden layers with nonlinear activations extend the functions a linear classifier can represent.

claims.note: The answer is supplied to the picture, not discovered by a network.

claims.claim: The three laps illustrate refinement rather than learned reasoning.
claims.how: Each lap chooses another stored bitmap level, with no attention, recurrent tensor update, or learned stopping rule.

sources.title: Universal Transformers
sources.says: Transformer computation can recur across depth, with an optional mechanism that adapts the number of updates.

simplified: The noise, coarse, nearly finished, and exact tile images are prepared stages. The lap count is fixed at three and is not chosen by difficulty.
